description: Quest deck for Let It Grow. 25 quests across 7 NPCs, including zone-specific exploration, biome, advanced, and community quests.

quests.title: Grandpa's Tomatoes
quests.description: Old Gus remembers a cherry tomato his grandfather used to grow — sweet as candy, red as sunset. He wants to see if you can coax that old variety back to life in your garden.
quests.acceptDialogue: Used to be a tomato my granddad grew. Small thing. Red as a barn door. Sweetest you ever tasted. Haven't seen one in years. Think you can find it? Grow me three. I'll know if they're right.
quests.progressDialogue: Back when I was small, those tomatoes came in by the bushel. You'll get there. Just takes patience. Soil doesn't hurry for nobody.
quests.completeDialogue: Well I'll be. That's the one. Smell that? That's summer, 1962. Here — take these pepper seeds. My granddad grew those too. Figured they ought to stay together.

outcomes.label: Share the seed with the block
outcomes.summary: The old tomato's seed goes around the neighborhood, one paper envelope at a time.

storyLog.label: Share the seed with the block
storyLog.summary: The old tomato's seed goes around the neighborhood, one paper envelope at a time.

echoes.line: Gus's grandfather's tomato is in half the yards on the block now. You started that.

outcomes.label: Keep the seed line pure
outcomes.summary: You bag and label the seed so the variety stays true to type.

storyLog.label: Keep the seed line pure
storyLog.summary: You bag and label the seed so the variety stays true to type.

echoes.line: Gus says you are keeping his grandfather's tomato true to type. That is real seed discipline.

quests.title: The Old Compost Method
quests.description: Gus's compost bin has seen better days. He swears his old layering method made the richest soil in the county. Help him restore it with fresh compost and some kale for green matter.
quests.acceptDialogue: Bin's falling apart. Used to make the best dirt you ever saw. Dark as coffee. Smelled like the forest floor after rain. Need two batches of compost and some kale for the green layer. You in?
quests.progressDialogue: Back when the bin was working, worms came from three yards over. They knew. Animals always know where the good soil is. Keep at it.
quests.completeDialogue: That's the stuff. Layers just right. Give it six weeks and this'll be black gold. You earned this — compost supplies, on me. And you learned something about soil today. That's worth more than seeds.

outcomes.label: Teach the layering to Jo
outcomes.summary: Gus's layering method goes into Jo's community pile.

storyLog.label: Teach the layering to Jo
storyLog.summary: Gus's layering method goes into Jo's community pile.

echoes.line: Jo's compost pile finally smells right. Word is Gus showed you, and you showed Jo.

outcomes.label: Keep Gus's bin going
outcomes.summary: You take a turn tending Gus's bin every week.

storyLog.label: Keep Gus's bin going
storyLog.summary: You take a turn tending Gus's bin every week.

echoes.line: Gus's compost readings jumped once you started turning that bin.

quests.title: Before the First Frost
quests.description: Winter is coming, and Gus knows the signs. He needs you to harvest five cold-weather crops before the frost kills them. The clock is ticking — once fall ends, they're gone.
quests.acceptDialogue: Frost's coming. I can feel it in my knees. We got carrots, beets, kale, broccoli, and turnips still in the ground. Pull them all before winter hits or we lose the lot. No second chances with frost.
quests.progressDialogue: Sky's getting grayer. Hurry it up. Used to be we had another week this time of year. Weather's not what it was. Get those crops in.
quests.completeDialogue: Every last one. That's how it's done. My dad would've said you've got farmer's hands. Here — rare seeds I've been saving. Didn't think I'd find someone worth giving them to.

outcomes.label: Cover the neighbors' beds too
outcomes.summary: You spend the last warm evening throwing frost cloth over the block's beds.

storyLog.label: Cover the neighbors' beds too
storyLog.summary: You spend the last warm evening throwing frost cloth over the block's beds.

echoes.line: Pat told me you covered half the street before the frost. People remember that.

outcomes.label: Save seed from the survivors
outcomes.summary: The crops that made it through get their seed saved for next year.

storyLog.label: Save seed from the survivors
storyLog.summary: The crops that made it through get their seed saved for next year.

echoes.line: That cold-hardy seed you saved from Gus's frost run. I want to scan it.

quests.title: The Prototype Sprinkler
quests.description: Maya's been sketching designs for a garden sprinkler system on napkins for weeks. She's got the blueprints — sort of — but needs someone to actually build the first prototype.
quests.acceptDialogue: OK so I've been thinking — well, more like obsessing — about irrigation efficiency, right? And I drew this sprinkler design on a napkin at breakfast, and — oh! I spilled coffee on it but the important parts survived — anyway, can you build one? Just one! The basic version. I need to see if the flow rate matches my calculations.
quests.progressDialogue: How's it going? Did you figure out the valve part? Because I was thinking — wait, no, finish the first version first. But ALSO I had this idea for a drip attachment that — no. Focus. Basic sprinkler. Then we iterate!
quests.completeDialogue: YOU BUILT IT! Let me see — oh wow, the spray pattern is actually better than I predicted! Here, take this — I call it the Smart Watering Can, it's got a — well, it's basically a regular can but I added a moisture sensor to the — you know what, just try it. You'll love it.

outcomes.label: Post the design for the block
outcomes.summary: Maya's napkin sketch becomes a printout on the notice board.

storyLog.label: Post the design for the block
storyLog.summary: Maya's napkin sketch becomes a printout on the notice board.

echoes.line: Every yard on the block has one of those spinners now. Maya's design, your hands.

outcomes.label: Keep the spare parts
outcomes.summary: You pocket the leftover lens and fittings for the next build.

storyLog.label: Keep the spare parts
storyLog.summary: You pocket the leftover lens and fittings for the next build.

echoes.line: Maya says you keep every spare part. She means it as a compliment.

quests.title: Soil Scanner Calibration
quests.description: Maya built a soil scanner but it needs real-world calibration data. Visit the meadow, riverside, and forest edge so she can compare readings across different soil compositions.
quests.acceptDialogue: So I built this soil scanner — don't ask how, I may have borrowed parts from a — anyway, it WORKS, theoretically, but I need field data from three different soil types to calibrate it. The meadow, the riverside, and the forest edge. Totally different mineral profiles. Oh! And take notes on the color? Or don't, I'll add a camera next version.
quests.progressDialogue: Did you get to all three spots yet? Because the calibration won't work unless — actually wait, even partial data could — no, I need all three. The riverside clay is completely different from the meadow loam and I need that contrast to set the baseline. Science!
quests.completeDialogue: Three zones! Three datasets! This is — hold on, let me punch these numbers — YES. The scanner works! PH, nitrogen, phosphorus, all reading clean. You earned this. Take the scanner. I already started building version two with a — actually, you don't want to know. Just take it.

outcomes.label: Post the soil map at the market
outcomes.summary: Maya's readings go up as a soil map anyone can use.

storyLog.label: Post the soil map at the market
storyLog.summary: Maya's readings go up as a soil map anyone can use.

echoes.line: That soil map you and Maya posted? Half my regulars are planting by it.

outcomes.label: Keep detailed field notes
outcomes.summary: You log every reading with the weather and the hour.

storyLog.label: Keep detailed field notes
storyLog.summary: You log every reading with the weather and the hour.

echoes.line: Maya showed me your field notes. Neat handwriting. Means you were paying attention.

quests.title: The Experimental Hybrid
quests.description: Maya has a wild theory about cross-pollinating cherry tomatoes and peppers to create a new hybrid variety. She needs you to plant both crops side by side and craft a hybrid seed.
quests.acceptDialogue: OK this is going to sound crazy — but what if we could cross a cherry tomato with a pepper? I've been reading about capsaicinoid transfer and lycopene expression and — oh! I found this old paper from 1987 that suggests — anyway, plant them next to each other, and I'll walk you through the seed grafting. This could be HUGE. Or a total disaster. Either way, data!
quests.progressDialogue: How are the plants looking? Are they flowering yet? Because the cross-pollination window is really narrow — like three days — and we need to time the — wait, did you plant them close enough? They need to be ADJACENT. The bees won't fly far in summer heat and — just check on them, OK?
quests.completeDialogue: A hybrid seed. An actual hybrid seed. Do you realize what we just — this is a brand new cultivar! Nobody's ever — well, probably someone has, but WE did it! Here, take these hybrid seeds. Grow them out. Document everything. I need to write this up. Where's my notebook? WHERE'S MY — oh, it's in my hand.

outcomes.label: Name the hybrid with the block
outcomes.summary: The block votes on a name for the cross. It is a silly name. It sticks.

storyLog.label: Name the hybrid with the block
storyLog.summary: The block votes on a name for the cross. It is a silly name. It sticks.

echoes.line: The hybrid is on my menu under the name the block picked. People order it just to say it.

outcomes.label: Grow it out until it breeds true
outcomes.summary: You commit a bed to growing the cross out until the seed breeds true.

storyLog.label: Grow it out until it breeds true
storyLog.summary: You commit a bed to growing the cross out until the seed breeds true.

echoes.line: Maya's cross is breeding true? That takes patience. Most folks quit at the second generation.

quests.title: Fresh Basil, Please
quests.description: Lila needs fresh basil for tonight's special. Not grocery store basil — real, garden-grown basil with actual flavor. Three bunches, and they'd better smell like something.
quests.acceptDialogue: I need basil. Three bunches. And I mean fresh. Not store-shelf fresh. Dawn-picked fresh. The kind where you bruise a leaf and the whole kitchen smells like summer in Genoa. Can you do that? Because the last person who brought me basil — I won't even talk about it. It was an insult to pesto.
quests.progressDialogue: Still waiting on that basil. Every hour it's not here, the leaves on MY plants get a little sadder. Sympathetic wilting. That's a real thing. I may have made it up. But the point stands — hurry.
quests.completeDialogue: Let me see. Let me smell. ...Yes. THAT is basil. You can taste the sun in these leaves. Here — take these herb seeds. Grow more. Grow different ones. A garden without herbs is just a vegetable warehouse.

outcomes.label: Bring an extra bunch for the crew
outcomes.summary: Lila's kitchen crew gets the extra bunch for family meal.

storyLog.label: Bring an extra bunch for the crew
storyLog.summary: Lila's kitchen crew gets the extra bunch for family meal.

echoes.line: Lila's crew still talks about the basil you brought for family meal.

outcomes.label: Let one plant bolt for seed
outcomes.summary: You leave one basil plant to flower and save its seed.

storyLog.label: Let one plant bolt for seed
storyLog.summary: You leave one basil plant to flower and save its seed.

echoes.line: Saw you let a basil go to flower. Good. The bees will thank you, and so will next year.

quests.title: The Perfect Salsa
quests.description: Lila is perfecting her fresh salsa recipe and needs garden-ripe ingredients. Tomatoes, peppers, cilantro, and onion — all from the same soil, all at peak ripeness.
quests.acceptDialogue: I'm making salsa. Not the jarred kind — the kind that makes you close your eyes and forget what month it is. I need two ripe tomatoes, two peppers with actual heat, one bunch of cilantro, and an onion with bite. Everything from your garden. Supermarket produce has no soul.
quests.progressDialogue: The mortar and pestle are ready. The lime is cut. I'm literally just standing here waiting for you. No pressure. But also — pressure. Flavor waits for no one.
quests.completeDialogue: Tomatoes — firm, good. Peppers — I can smell the capsaicin. Cilantro — bright, not bolted. Onion — oh, that'll make someone cry, and I mean that as the highest compliment. Take this recipe card. You've earned it. Share it with someone who deserves it.

outcomes.label: Serve it at the block party
outcomes.summary: The salsa goes out in a big bowl on Pat's porch.

storyLog.label: Serve it at the block party
storyLog.summary: The salsa goes out in a big bowl on Pat's porch.

echoes.line: That salsa at Pat's party had some kick. Your peppers?

outcomes.label: Write down the ripeness tests
outcomes.summary: You and Lila write down how to tell each ingredient is ready.

storyLog.label: Write down the ripeness tests
storyLog.summary: You and Lila write down how to tell each ingredient is ready.

echoes.line: Lila showed me your ripeness notes. That is basically a sensor spec.

quests.title: Mom's Secret Recipe
quests.description: Lila brings a handwritten family recipe card — a sauce that takes eight ingredients, all garden-fresh. She has not made it for the block before. This is personal, and every ingredient has to be perfect.
quests.acceptDialogue: This is my family's recipe. We do not make it for just anyone. I need tomatoes, basil, peppers, onion, carrot, and garlic — all from the garden. Not because it tastes better. Because the garden has to be part of it. Every ingredient matters. Don't bring me anything you wouldn't eat raw, standing in the dirt.
quests.progressDialogue: I keep reading the handwriting on the card. 'Fresh' is underlined three times. Garlic is spelled wrong. I'm not changing it. Just bring me what I asked for. Take your time. But not too much time. Fall doesn't last forever.
quests.completeDialogue: Everything's here. All of it, perfect. I can smell her kitchen already. ...Thank you. I mean it. Here — these seeds are rare. I've been saving them for someone who understands that food isn't just food. It's memory. It's people. You get that.

outcomes.label: Cook it for the whole block
outcomes.summary: The sauce gets made in a pot big enough for everyone.

storyLog.label: Cook it for the whole block
storyLog.summary: The sauce gets made in a pot big enough for everyone.

echoes.line: Had a bowl of that sauce. Tasted like somebody's kitchen from forty years back.

outcomes.label: Keep the recipe card safe
outcomes.summary: The card goes in your journal, copied out in your own hand.

storyLog.label: Keep the recipe card safe
storyLog.summary: The card goes in your journal, copied out in your own hand.

echoes.line: Lila trusted you with the card itself. She does not do that.

quests.title: Weekend Watering
quests.description: Pat's heading out of town for the weekend and needs someone to water their garden. Visit the neighborhood and make sure nothing wilts while they're gone.
quests.acceptDialogue: Hey neighbor! I'm visiting my sister this weekend — could you pop over and water my garden? It's just the front beds, nothing fancy. But my sunflowers are FINALLY about to bloom and I'd hate to lose them to the heat.
quests.progressDialogue: How's it going over there? I keep checking my weather app. It says hot and dry. Please tell me my sunflowers are OK. I'm trusting you with my babies!
quests.completeDialogue: Everything's alive! And are those — did my sunflowers BLOOM? You're the best neighbor ever. Here, take some of this plant matter I've been saving. Least I can do!

outcomes.label: Water the whole row
outcomes.summary: You water Pat's beds and the two yards next door.

storyLog.label: Water the whole row
storyLog.summary: You water Pat's beds and the two yards next door.

echoes.line: Pat came back to a whole row of happy beds and told everyone.

outcomes.label: Leave Pat a watering schedule
outcomes.summary: You leave a note on how much each bed drank.

storyLog.label: Leave Pat a watering schedule
storyLog.summary: You leave a note on how much each bed drank.

echoes.line: Pat's watering schedule? I would like a copy. That is good data.

quests.title: Bee-Friendly Garden
quests.description: Sam keeps bees and wants to plant companion flowers nearby to help the hive thrive. Marigolds and nasturtiums are perfect — bright, fragrant, and full of pollen.
quests.acceptDialogue: My bees need more forage — the clover field got mowed last week and they're struggling. Could you plant some marigolds and a nasturtium near the garden? The bees love those bright colors, and nasturtium nectar makes the most amazing honey.
quests.progressDialogue: The bees are out there looking for flowers every morning. Poor things come back with barely anything. How are those plantings coming along?
quests.completeDialogue: Flowers in the ground! The bees will find them by tomorrow, I guarantee it. Here — fresh honey from last season's harvest. Consider it an advance payment from the bees themselves.

outcomes.label: Plant a border for the whole street
outcomes.summary: Marigolds go in along the curb for every hive and yard.

storyLog.label: Plant a border for the whole street
storyLog.summary: Marigolds go in along the curb for every hive and yard.

echoes.line: Sam's flower border runs the whole street now. Bees everywhere. Good for the tomatoes.

outcomes.label: Track which flowers the bees work
outcomes.summary: You and Sam log which blooms the bees visit most.

storyLog.label: Track which flowers the bees work
storyLog.summary: You and Sam log which blooms the bees visit most.

echoes.line: Sam says your bee log shows the nasturtiums win. I want that dataset.

quests.title: Compost Contribution
quests.description: Jo is building a community compost pile and needs plant matter contributions. Any five harvested crops will do — it all breaks down the same.
quests.acceptDialogue: I'm starting a community compost pile in the back corner of the lot. Good for the neighborhood, good for the soil. But I need green matter to get it started. Got any crops you can spare? Five of anything will do. It all turns into dirt eventually.
quests.progressDialogue: The compost pile's looking a little sad right now. Just a pile of leaves and cardboard. It needs the good stuff — garden scraps, crop waste. Bring me what you've got!
quests.completeDialogue: That's what I'm talking about! This pile is going to cook. Give it a few weeks and we'll have the richest compost on the block. Take this fertilizer — consider it the first dividend from our little compost investment.

outcomes.label: Open the pile to everyone
outcomes.summary: Jo's pile gets a sign: bring scraps, take compost.

storyLog.label: Open the pile to everyone
storyLog.summary: Jo's pile gets a sign: bring scraps, take compost.

echoes.line: Jo's pile takes my kitchen scraps now. Your idea, I hear.

outcomes.label: Measure the pile's heat
outcomes.summary: You check the pile temperature until it cooks properly.

storyLog.label: Measure the pile's heat
storyLog.summary: You check the pile temperature until it cooks properly.

echoes.line: Jo's pile is running hot now. You measured it? Smart.

quests.title: Bird Census
quests.description: Robin is conducting a neighborhood bird census and needs help spotting species in different habitats. Visit the meadow, riverside, and forest edge to record what you see.
quests.acceptDialogue: I'm doing a bird count for the neighborhood nature group. We need observations from three different habitats — the meadow, the riverside, and the forest edge. Different birds, different zones. Grab your binoculars. Well, grab your eyes. Binoculars are optional but strongly encouraged.
quests.progressDialogue: How many zones have you visited? Each habitat has different species. The meadow has sparrows and larks, the riverside has kingfishers, and the forest edge — that's where the warblers hide. Don't rush it. Birds can tell when you're impatient.
quests.completeDialogue: Three habitats surveyed! Let me see your notes — oh, wonderful. A kingfisher at the riverside? That's the first sighting this season. You've got a good eye. Here, take these wildflower seeds. Plant them and you'll bring even more birds to the garden.

outcomes.label: Hang feeders along the route
outcomes.summary: Robin's census route gets feeders so the count keeps going.

storyLog.label: Hang feeders along the route
storyLog.summary: Robin's census route gets feeders so the count keeps going.

echoes.line: Robin's feeders are full of finches, right outside my windows.

outcomes.label: Keep a careful census record
outcomes.summary: Every sighting goes in the log with the time and the place.

storyLog.label: Keep a careful census record
storyLog.summary: Every sighting goes in the log with the time and the place.

echoes.line: Robin's census sheet is in your handwriting. Very clean.

quests.title: Map the Meadow
quests.description: Explore the meadow zone and discover all three foraging spots. Robin wants a full survey of what grows wild out there.
quests.acceptDialogue: The meadow's full of surprises if you know where to look. I need someone to map out the foraging spots — wildflower patches, herb clusters, rock piles. Find all three and report back.
quests.progressDialogue: Still mapping? Take your time. The meadow reveals itself slowly. Look near the old fence line and along the creek bank.
quests.completeDialogue: All three spots documented! This is exactly what the nature group needed. You've got a real eye for the wild places. Here — some rare seeds I've been saving.

outcomes.label: Mark a trail for the neighbors
outcomes.summary: You stake small markers so others can find the patches.

storyLog.label: Mark a trail for the neighbors
storyLog.summary: You stake small markers so others can find the patches.

echoes.line: Somebody marked the meadow trails. Robin says it was you.

outcomes.label: Leave the patches unmarked
outcomes.summary: You map the spots but leave the meadow as you found it.

storyLog.label: Leave the patches unmarked
storyLog.summary: You map the spots but leave the meadow as you found it.

echoes.line: Your meadow survey, and not a single stake in the ground. Respect.

quests.title: River Crossing
quests.description: Old Gus mentions a fishing spot he used to visit by the river. Help him remember the path and find the old crossing.
quests.acceptDialogue: Used to fish down by the river. Every Sunday. Path's overgrown now. If you can find where it starts — behind the big oak in the neighborhood — I'll tell you the rest.
quests.progressDialogue: Still looking? The oak's on the east side. Path used to go through the tall grass. Might need to push through some brambles.
quests.completeDialogue: You found it. The old crossing. Haven't seen that in years. River's still running the same way. Here — the path is yours now. Go whenever you want.

outcomes.label: Clear the path for everyone
outcomes.summary: The brambles come out and the old crossing opens to the block.

storyLog.label: Clear the path for everyone
storyLog.summary: The brambles come out and the old crossing opens to the block.

echoes.line: I take the river path for watercress now. Gus says you cleared it.

outcomes.label: Keep the crossing quiet
outcomes.summary: You and Gus agree the fishing spot stays between the two of you.

storyLog.label: Keep the crossing quiet
storyLog.summary: You and Gus agree the fishing spot stays between the two of you.

echoes.line: Gus will not tell me where his fishing spot is. He says you know. Fine.

quests.title: The Greenhouse Key
quests.description: The old greenhouse needs a new panel before it can be used again. Maya thinks you're skilled enough to build one — if you've reached Crafting level 5.
quests.acceptDialogue: Okay okay okay — so the greenhouse? Totally fixable. You just need to craft a greenhouse panel. I drew up the plans — well, most of them. The important parts. Probably. You've got the skills for it!
quests.progressDialogue: Panel's not done yet? You need crystal shards and scrap metal. Check the forest for shards — oh! And Maya's tip: hit the rocks at an angle. More efficient. Probably.
quests.completeDialogue: YOU BUILT IT! Look at that panel! It's beautiful. It's functional. It's — okay it's a little crooked but that adds character. Greenhouse is all yours now!

outcomes.label: Open the benches to the block
outcomes.summary: The greenhouse gets a sign-up sheet for winter benches.

storyLog.label: Open the benches to the block
storyLog.summary: The greenhouse gets a sign-up sheet for winter benches.

echoes.line: I have a winter bench in the greenhouse for herbs now. Thank you.

outcomes.label: Tune the climate first
outcomes.summary: You spend a week dialing in heat and vents before anything goes in.

storyLog.label: Tune the climate first
storyLog.summary: You spend a week dialing in heat and vents before anything goes in.

echoes.line: Maya says you will not let a plant into that greenhouse till the vents are right. Good instinct.

quests.title: Watercress for Lila
quests.description: Lila needs fresh watercress from the riverside for a special stew recipe. Only wild-foraged will do — nothing from a garden bed.
quests.acceptDialogue: I'm working on a forager's stew. Old family recipe. But it needs real watercress — riverside watercress. The kind that grows where the water runs cold. Bring me three bunches. Fresh. Not wilted. Not 'it was fresh yesterday.' Fresh.
quests.progressDialogue: The watercress? Still waiting. Remember — riverside only. I can taste the difference. Don't test me.
quests.completeDialogue: Now THAT is watercress. Feel the crunch? See the color? This is going straight into the stew. Here — you've earned the recipe. Make it yourself sometime.

outcomes.label: Make it a stew night
outcomes.summary: Lila turns the watercress into a pot of stew for the neighbors.

storyLog.label: Make it a stew night
storyLog.summary: Lila turns the watercress into a pot of stew for the neighbors.

echoes.line: Lila's forager stew. Have not had watercress like that since I was a boy.

outcomes.label: Leave the patch to regrow
outcomes.summary: You take only what Lila needs and leave the rest of the bed.

storyLog.label: Leave the patch to regrow
storyLog.summary: You take only what Lila needs and leave the rest of the bed.

echoes.line: The watercress bed came back thick this year. Light harvesting works.

quests.title: Mushroom Log Inoculation
quests.description: Gus wants to set up shiitake logs in the forest edge. He needs wood and compost to get started, and a hand with the heavy lifting.
quests.acceptDialogue: Forest's got the right shade for mushrooms. Did this with my grandfather. Need four good logs and some compost to pack around the base. You bring the materials, I'll show you how it's done.
quests.progressDialogue: Got the wood and compost yet? Oak's best for the logs. And the compost needs to be mature — none of that half-rotted stuff.
quests.completeDialogue: That's it. Logs are set. Give it a few weeks and you'll see the first pins coming through. Here — take some spores. Start your own logs if you want. My grandfather would've liked you.

outcomes.label: Inoculate extra logs for neighbors
outcomes.summary: A few extra logs go to Sam's and Jo's shady corners.

storyLog.label: Inoculate extra logs for neighbors
storyLog.summary: A few extra logs go to Sam's and Jo's shady corners.

echoes.line: Sam brought me shiitake off a log you inoculated. Beautiful.

outcomes.label: Keep a spawn culture going
outcomes.summary: You keep a jar of spawn alive for next season's logs.

storyLog.label: Keep a spawn culture going
storyLog.summary: You keep a jar of spawn alive for next season's logs.

echoes.line: Gus says your spawn jar is still alive. That is not easy.

quests.title: The Vanilla Challenge
quests.description: Maya dares you to grow a vanilla orchid to full maturity in the greenhouse. It's a long game — multiple seasons — but the reward is legendary.
quests.acceptDialogue: So I've been reading about vanilla orchids and — okay don't laugh — but they take FOREVER to grow. Like, multiple seasons. But imagine! Fresh vanilla! In our greenhouse! I dare you. No — I DOUBLE dare you.
quests.progressDialogue: How's the vanilla? Still growing? It's so slow! I keep checking mine and — wait, I shouldn't tell you about mine. This is YOUR challenge. Keep going!
quests.completeDialogue: YOU DID IT! A full vanilla orchid! Do you know how rare that is?! The smell alone — okay I'm crying a little. This is the best day. Here, take this. You've earned something legendary.

outcomes.label: Invite the block to see the bloom
outcomes.summary: The orchid opens for one day and half the block comes to look.

storyLog.label: Invite the block to see the bloom
storyLog.summary: The orchid opens for one day and half the block comes to look.

echoes.line: Saw that orchid bloom. Did not think a vanilla would flower around here.

outcomes.label: Hand pollinate it and log every step
outcomes.summary: You pollinate the flower by hand and record each step.

storyLog.label: Hand pollinate it and log every step
storyLog.summary: You pollinate the flower by hand and record each step.

echoes.line: Maya says your vanilla pod is hand pollinated. I want that pod.

quests.title: Prairie Restoration
quests.description: Sam wants to restore soil health in the meadow by planting nitrogen-fixing wild clover. Five plants should make a real difference.
quests.acceptDialogue: The meadow soil's been depleted for years. Wild clover fixes nitrogen naturally — it's like free fertilizer from nature. Could you plant five clover patches out there? The whole ecosystem will thank you.
quests.progressDialogue: How many clover plants are in? Each one is helping the soil recover. The bees love them too — win-win.
quests.completeDialogue: Five clover patches! The meadow's already looking healthier. You can actually see the difference in the soil color. Here — I found this rare earth mineral while digging. You should have it.

outcomes.label: Hold a meadow work day
outcomes.summary: Sam and the neighbors plant clover together on a Saturday.

storyLog.label: Hold a meadow work day
storyLog.summary: Sam and the neighbors plant clover together on a Saturday.

echoes.line: Heard about the meadow work day. The clover is coming in thick.

outcomes.label: Test the soil as it recovers
outcomes.summary: You check the meadow soil each season to see the clover work.

storyLog.label: Test the soil as it recovers

quests.title: Maya's Masterpiece
quests.description: Maya's ultimate invention: a seed hybridizer that can crossbreed crops. She needs a master crafter she trusts to build it.
quests.acceptDialogue: Okay. This is the big one. I've been designing this for — honestly? Years. A seed hybridizer. It can CROSSBREED crops. But the build is incredibly precise. I need someone at Crafting level 7 who I trust completely. That's you. No pressure. Okay, some pressure.
quests.progressDialogue: The hybridizer needs crystal shards, mechanisms, AND rare earth. I know that's a lot. But think about what we're building! NEW CROPS. From EXISTING CROPS. Science!
quests.completeDialogue: It's... it's perfect. Better than my blueprints. You actually improved the calibration mechanism — I see what you did there. This changes everything. You can crossbreed crops now. Go make something the world's never seen.

outcomes.label: Hold open hours at the hybridizer
outcomes.summary: Maya sets hours so neighbors can try crosses with you.

storyLog.label: Hold open hours at the hybridizer
storyLog.summary: Maya sets hours so neighbors can try crosses with you.

echoes.line: Maya has folks lined up at that machine. You built it right.

outcomes.label: Calibrate it before anyone uses it
outcomes.summary: You run test crosses until the results repeat.

storyLog.label: Calibrate it before anyone uses it
storyLog.summary: You run test crosses until the results repeat.

echoes.line: Maya says the hybridizer does not run a cross until you sign off. Careful of you.

quests.title: Gus's Legacy Garden
quests.description: Gus wants to recreate his grandfather's exact garden layout. He remembers every plant, every position. This is deeply personal to him.
quests.acceptDialogue: My grandfather had a garden. Perfect garden. Tomatoes here. Basil there. Marigolds along the edge. I remember it like it was yesterday. I want to see it again. One more time. Can you build it?
quests.progressDialogue: The tomatoes go in the center. Basil right next to them. Marigolds on the border — he always said they kept the bad bugs out. Peppers on the sunny side. Carrots in the shade of the tomatoes.
quests.completeDialogue: ... That's it. That's his garden. Looks just like I remember. Thank you. I don't say that often. Here — his trowel recipe. And some seeds he saved. They've been in my family for generations. Take care of them.

outcomes.label: Plant it with Gus
outcomes.summary: You and Gus put in every plant together, him pointing, you digging.

storyLog.label: Plant it with Gus
storyLog.summary: You and Gus put in every plant together, him pointing, you digging.

echoes.line: Gus walked me through his grandfather's garden yesterday. He was smiling the whole time.

outcomes.label: Draw the plan for the archive
outcomes.summary: You draw the layout to scale so it outlasts both of you.

storyLog.label: Draw the plan for the archive
storyLog.summary: You draw the layout to scale so it outlasts both of you.

echoes.line: Your drawing of Gus's legacy garden is going in the library archive. I made sure.

quests.title: Lila's Cookbook
quests.description: Lila wants to complete a full cookbook with ingredients from every recipe. This is her life's work — and she needs your help to finish it.
quests.acceptDialogue: I've been writing this cookbook for ten years. Ten years of recipes, techniques, stories. But I need every recipe completed with fresh ingredients. Every single one. You've helped me before. Will you help me finish this?
quests.progressDialogue: How many recipes have you sourced? I need ingredients for all eight. Fresh. Seasonal. Perfect. This cookbook doesn't accept 'good enough.'
quests.completeDialogue: Every recipe. Every ingredient. This cookbook is complete. I'm putting your name in the acknowledgments. Right after my grandmother's. That's the highest honor I give. Thank you.

outcomes.label: Print a community edition
outcomes.summary: Every neighbor who grew an ingredient gets a page credit.

storyLog.label: Print a community edition
storyLog.summary: Every neighbor who grew an ingredient gets a page credit.

echoes.line: My name is in Lila's cookbook. Page twelve. Do not tell anyone I read it.

quests.title: Market Day
quests.description: Pat's organizing a big market day and needs someone to help fill the stalls. Trade 10 items at the market square to make it a success.
quests.acceptDialogue: Market day's coming up and we're short on traders! If you could bring 10 items to trade — seeds, tools, produce, anything — we'll have the best market the neighborhood's ever seen.
quests.progressDialogue: How many trades so far? We need the stalls full. The more variety, the better the market. People come from all over for a good market day.
quests.completeDialogue: Ten trades! The market was a huge success. People are already asking when the next one is. You made this happen. Here — the other traders pooled some rare materials as a thank-you.

quests.title: Festival Champion
quests.description: Complete all four seasonal festival activities in a single year to earn the Festival Champion trophy. Jo's been trying for years — can you do it?
quests.acceptDialogue: Every year I try to hit all four festivals and every year something comes up. Spring Bloom, Summer Surge, Harvest Week, Winter Dormancy — all four in one year. Think you can do it? I'll be cheering you on!
quests.progressDialogue: How many festivals have you completed this year? Remember — all four, same year. Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter. No skipping!
quests.completeDialogue: ALL FOUR! You did it! Festival Champion! I've never even gotten past three! This trophy is yours — and honestly? The whole neighborhood's going to score a little better with you inspiring everyone. Five percent better, I'd say.
